short: how many children an index page points at. hundreds in a b-tree, which is why it stays three or four levels deep.
a key on an inner b-tree page that says where a child page's range starts. a copy, not the row's own entry.
the first item on every non-rightmost b-tree page: an upper bound for the page's keys, pointing at no row.
the first item of an inner b-tree page: a child pointer with no key, for everything below the first separator.
page 0 of an index: where the root is, how tall the tree is, or a hash index's bucket masks. bt_metap reads it.
what happens when an index page is full: part of it moves to a new page, linked in beside it, with a new downlink above.
every b-tree page's pointer to its right neighbour on the same level. lets a reader follow a split it didn't see.
the textbook way to descend a b-tree safely: latch the child before releasing the parent, keep ancestors while a split could reach them.
one index key followed by a sorted list of heap addresses, instead of one entry per row.
postgres 13+: merging b-tree entries with equal keys into posting lists, just before a leaf would split.
postgres 14+: before a leaf splits, deleting entries whose row versions are dead, left by updates that didn't change the key.
a hint bit on an index entry: its row is dead to everyone, so the entry can be removed without checking the heap again.
one slot of a hash index: a primary page plus any overflow pages, holding the entries whose hash picks it.
an extra page chained to a full hash bucket. many duplicates make long chains.
growing a hash table one bucket at a time, rehashing only the one bucket that splits. how postgres's hash index grows.
an index with one entry per element (word, tag, key) listing the rows that contain it. GIN is one.
a GIN key's row addresses stored as a b-tree of their own, once there are too many for a posting list.
an unsorted list of new GIN entries, merged into the index in bulk later. on by default with fastupdate.
the smallest rectangle around a set of shapes or points. GiST's inner pages store one per child.
splitting space into parts that never overlap, as SP-GiST does: quadtrees, k-d trees, radix trees.
a run of table pages BRIN summarizes as one entry, 128 by default.
log-structured merge tree: writes go to a memtable, flushed to immutable sorted files that compaction merges.
the sorted in-memory buffer an LSM tree writes to first, flushed to disk when full.
sorted string table: an immutable file of sorted keys an LSM tree writes when it flushes or compacts.
an LSM tree's background merge of sorted files into bigger ones, dropping overwritten values and tombstones.
a bit array and k hashes that answers definitely not or maybe. about 1% false positives at 10 bits per key.
pages or files read per lookup. with write and space amplification, the trade every storage engine makes.
hierarchical navigable small world: a layered graph searched greedily, for approximate nearest neighbours.
a vector index that clusters vectors into lists and scans only the nearest few (ivfflat.probes).
the fraction of the true nearest neighbours an approximate search returns.
